notes:
Summary: enterprise evaluation for Reserved GPU pools across NA + EU with warm-standby headroom.
- Business need: low-latency reranking + per-user personalization for ad auctions; strict cost control.
- Traffic profile: bursty bid windows (10–60s), steady background personalization queries, peak concurrency during campaign launches (x10 baseline).
- Latency SLOs requested: p50 < 35ms, p95 < 120ms for 512-token generation paths; p95 < 40ms for emb/rerank endpoints.
- Throughput goals: sustained 800k tokens/sec global (mixed traffic) with regional peak 300k tokens/sec NA, 200k tokens/sec EU.
- GPU preferences: H100-preferred for long-context chat/rerank; supports A100 fallback for cost-sensitive routes.
- Routing/fallback: want policy-based routing by tenant region + automatic fallback to quantized variants when latency > SLO or capacity constraints.
- Reserve planning ask: dedicated reserved pools in NA + EU, multi-AZ distribution, warm-standby equal to 20% peak for immediate failover, plus 10% cross-region burst allowance.
- Failover model: active-active with local primary; passive warm-standby in second region (GPU pre-warmed with model weights, prefix cache priming during low-traffic hours).
- Acceptance criteria for POC: 1) sustain 80% of target throughput for 30m without QoS degradation, 2) failover cutover under 45s with <5% error increase, 3) token-cost per 1M under quoted threshold.
- Security/compliance: require SOC2 attestation, KMS integration, SSO for engineer access, and audit logs retention 1 year. EU traffic must be processed in EU region.
- Quote ask: line-item pricing for base reserved capacity + warm-standby + cross-region bandwidth and burst credits.
- AE notes: excellent engagement from infra team; quoted latency numbers pulled from internal benchmark (see drive deck).
- SE notes (Priya): recommended kernel-level optimizations, aggressive KV cache for personalization queries, recommend Redwood Optimize run to suggest batching/quant profiles.
- Customer quote: "We need predictable tail latency during peak auctions — a surprise 200ms p95 kills ROI."
- Meetings: kickoff 2026-02-12 (discovery), technical deep-dive 2026-02-26, dedicated demo 2026-03-04 (PR/latency walk-through).
- Open items: legal redline on data residency, exact failover RTO/RPO commitments in SLA, final GPU SKU mix decision (H100 vs A100).
